jp.title: 竜の谷の小さな店と庭師の日々
jp.text:
古びた石畳に刻まれた風化の跡が、まるで過去を物語っているかのようだった。私はその瓦礫の上に座り込み、手元にある錆びついた鋏を磨き始めた。竜の谷と呼ばれるこの辺境の地では、時が止まったかのような静寂が流れている。人々が忙しく動き回る都市とは違い、ここでは大地の呼吸を感じながら日々を送ることができた。

「またそんなところでぼんやりしているのか？」

隣から声がした。振り返ると、赤い髪をした少女が手を差し伸べている。彼女の名はリナ。竜の鱗を持つ種族の末裔であり、この店を継いだばかりの店主である。彼女の瞳には、かつての王族としての誇りと、今生きるための穏やかな決意が宿っている。

「そうさ。今日は土の状態が良いみたいだからな」

私は微笑みながら答えた。庭師として過ごす毎日の中で、植物たちの成長を見守ることは、何よりの喜びだった。しかし、ある日、谷の奥深くから不吉な気配が漂ってきた。それは、昔ここで失われた伝説の宝物に関する噂だった。人々はそれを求める旅に出ようとするが、私はそれを拒んだ。なぜなら、その場所には大切な記憶が存在し、それを壊してはいけないと考えていたからだ。

だが、暴走した魔導装置が谷を揺らし、私の店の屋根まで崩れ落ちそうになった時、リナが駆けつけてくれた。二人は協力して修理を行い、谷の平穏を守り抜いた。事件の後、私は改めてこの場所での生活の意味を悟った。竜の谷の小さな店は、単なる商売の場ではなく、多くの人々が集い、交流し、安らぎを得るための聖域なのである。私たちはこれからも、この地で穏やかに、しかし確かに生きていく。それが私の選んだ道であり、最も幸せな人生であった。
jp.translation_en:
The weathered marks carved into the old cobblestones seemed to tell of the past. I sat down on the rubble and began polishing the rusty shears in my hands. In this frontier land called the Dragon Valley, a silence flows as if time itself had stopped. Unlike the cities where people bustle about, here I could spend my days feeling the earth breathe.

"Spacing out in a place like that again?"

A voice came from beside me. When I turned, a red-haired girl was holding out her hand. Her name was Rina. A descendant of a race with dragon scales, she had only just inherited this shop. In her eyes lived the pride of the royal line she once belonged to, and a calm resolve to live in the present.

"That's right. The soil looks good today."

I answered with a smile. Watching the plants grow, day after day as a gardener, was my greatest joy. But one day an ominous presence drifted up from deep inside the valley: rumors of a legendary treasure lost here long ago. People set out to seek it, but I refused, because I believed precious memories rested in that place and must not be destroyed.

Yet when a runaway magical device shook the valley and even the roof of my shop threatened to collapse, Rina came running. The two of us worked together on the repairs and protected the peace of the valley to the end. After the incident, I understood anew what living here meant. The little shop in the Dragon Valley is not just a place of business; it is a sanctuary where many people gather, meet and find rest. From now on too, we will live here quietly, but surely. That is the path I chose, and the happiest life there could be.

jp.title: 落第した書庫番と呪われた誓約
jp.text:
「また、失敗か……」

　静寂に包まれた『忘却の書庫』の最深部で、私は小さく呟いた。指先から伝わる冷たい石の感触が、私の震える心をなだめる代わりに、深く刺さるような痛みを伴う。

　私はこの巨大な図書館の管理を務める者だが、魔力測定の儀式において『落第』という烙印を押されてしまった。本来なら、この世界の知識を守り、災厄を封じるための聖なる器となるはずだったはずだ。しかし、私の魔力は枯渇しており、封印すべき呪いは一つも解けなかった。

　重苦しい空気の中で、棚の奥から黒い霧のようなものが這い出してきた。それは古の罪人たちが残した怨念であり、私が守るべき『禁忌』そのものだ。霧が形を成し始めると、そこには歪んだ影の姿があった。

「お前か……落ちこぼれの書庫番め」

　影が低く唸る。その声は、千の耳鳴りのように私の脳内に響き渡った。私は必死に両手を広げ、失われた魔力を無理やり引き出そうとするが、返ってくるのは虚無だけだった。

「お願いだ、ここで止めてくれ」

　私は膝をつき、地面に額をつけた。逃げ場はない。この書庫が崩壊すれば、世界中の歴史が霧の中に消えてしまう。私はただの管理人ではなく、この場所を守る最後の砦なのだ。

　絶望が胸を締め付ける。ならば、せめてこの命だけでも捧げよう。

　私は目を閉じ、魂の底にある、誰にも見せないほどの純粋な願いを込めた。それが、かつて祖師から受け継いだ、呪いとも呼べる契約だった。

「誓う……この身を、書庫の守護者として捧げよう！」

　轟音と共に、私の体が光に包まれた。悲鳴のような叫びが喉元まで上がろうとしたが、すぐに声は濁流に飲み込まれた。視界が白く染まり、痛みよりも先に、圧倒的な力の奔流が全身を駆け抜けていく。

　影の怪物たちは、突如として現れた巨大な障壁に阻まれ、悲鳴を上げて霧散していった。それらは物理的な敵ではなく、精神的な腐敗物だからだ。私の肉体が、それらを拒絶する壁となったのである。

　やがて、光が収まったとき、そこには静かな書庫が残っていた。怪物の痕跡はなく、棚も、床も、すべてが元の平穏を取り戻している。

　だが、私の身体はもう、人間のものではなかった。

　私は背伸びをしようとしたが、関節が軋む音は金属のように硬い。肌は冷たく、透明感のある青白い輝きを放っていた。手足からは魔力の粒子が零れ落ち、まるで生きた宝石のように瞬いている。

　鏡はないが、自分がどうなったかは分かった。私は今や、呪われた誓約によって、この書庫そのものの一部となってしまったのだ。

「……これで、よかったのか」

　私は、自らの声の響きを聞きながら、ふっと微笑んだ。落第した書庫番としての生涯は、ここで幕を閉じた。

　しかし、これは終わりではない。私はもう、物理的な制約を持たない。書庫の隅々まで、あらゆる場所に存在できる。誰かが危険に晒されたとき、私はその背後に立ち、目に見えない守護者として彼らを救うだろう。

　たとえ形を変えても、私の役割は終わらない。

　私は再び、静まり返った書庫の闇へと溶け込んでいった。次は、誰かの涙を拭い、失われた知識を繋ぎ止めるために。
jp.translation_en:
"A failure, again..."

In the deepest part of the silent Archive of Oblivion, I murmured to myself. The cold touch of the stone under my fingertips did not calm my trembling heart; it stung instead.

I am the keeper of this vast library, yet in the ceremony of measuring magic I was branded a failure. I was supposed to become a sacred vessel that guards the world's knowledge and seals away calamity. But my mana had run dry, and not one of the curses I was meant to seal could I undo.

In the heavy air, something like black mist crept out from the back of the shelves. It was the grudge left by sinners of old, the very Taboo I was meant to guard. As the mist took shape, a warped shadow appeared.

"So it's you... the washout archive keeper."

The shadow growled low. Its voice echoed inside my head like a thousand ringing ears. I spread my arms desperately and tried to force out the magic I had lost, but only emptiness answered.

"Please, stop it here."

I fell to my knees and pressed my forehead to the floor. There was nowhere to run. If this archive collapsed, the history of the whole world would vanish into the mist. I was not merely its caretaker; I was the last fortress guarding this place.

Despair tightened around my chest. Then at least let me offer this life.

I closed my eyes and poured into it the purest wish at the bottom of my soul, one I had never shown anyone. It was a pact, one you could even call a curse, handed down to me from my master's master.

"I swear... I offer this body as guardian of the archive!"

With a roar, my body was wrapped in light. A scream tried to rise into my throat, but my voice was swallowed at once by the torrent. My vision turned white, and before any pain, an overwhelming surge of power rushed through my whole body.

The shadow monsters were stopped by a giant barrier that appeared out of nowhere, and they shrieked and dissolved. They were not physical enemies but spiritual rot. My body had become the wall that rejected them.

When the light finally faded, only the quiet archive remained. No trace of the monsters; the shelves and the floor had all returned to their old peace.

But my body was no longer human.

I tried to stretch, but my joints creaked, hard as metal. My skin was cold and gave off a translucent, pale-blue glow. Particles of mana spilled from my hands and feet, twinkling like living jewels.

There was no mirror, but I knew what I had become. Through the cursed pact, I was now a part of the archive itself.

"...Was this for the best?"

Listening to the sound of my own voice, I smiled faintly. My life as a failed archive keeper ended here.

But this is not the end. I no longer have any physical limits. I can exist in every corner of the archive. When someone is in danger, I will stand behind them and save them as an unseen guardian.

Even if my form has changed, my role does not end.

I melted back into the darkness of the hushed archive. Next time, to wipe away someone's tears and to hold lost knowledge together.

jp.title: 霧の峡谷で始める付与術師のスローライフ
jp.passage:
「人間は、寿命という名の砂時計を気にしすぎて生きている」

私は窓の外に浮かぶ、静寂を纏った霧の谷間を見つめながら、そう呟いた。
私の指先には、誰にも見えない微かな光が宿っている。それは魔力ではなく、もっと根源的な、世界そのものが吐き出す息吹のようなもの。付与術師としての資質は、私がまだこの世のものではない頃に刻み込まれた。

私は骨でも魂でもない。かつて存在した何かが、形を変えて残した「痕跡」だ。
肉体的な苦痛も、空腹も感じない。代わりに、周囲の気配を五感以上に鋭く感知できる。
jp.text:
特に、この霧の峡谷『ミストラル・デイル』において。

ここは地図にも載らない、風と雲が常に交錯する場所だ。表の世界の人々は、ここを「呪われた死地」と呼んで避けて通る。だが、私にとっては天国に近い。なぜなら、ここでは誰も私の正体など知る由もないから。

「……また、あの音がするわ」

胸の奥、胸郭がないはずの場所に、かすかな違和感が走った。
付与された古い道具たちが、無意識のうちに警告音を鳴らしているのだ。
これは災いの予兆ではない。ただ、ただ、誰かが近くにいることを知らせる信号だ。

私は立ち上がり、机の上の茶器（もちろん、温める必要のない金属製の器だが）に手をかけた。
視線を床から遠ざけ、部屋の中央にある小さな庭へと移す。そこには、霧の中からせっかく育て上げた、青白い花々が咲いている。
付与の魔法は、花に力を与え、枯れないように保つためだけに使われている。それ以上の目的はない。それが私の望むスローライフの定義だった。

しかし、その花々の茎に絡みつくように、黒い影が蠢いているのが見えた。

「……あ、あったわね」

声に出さずとも、相手は確実に私の存在を認識しているだろう。
霧の向こう側、石造りの廃墟のような建物の方角から、一人の男が現れた。
彼は黒いマントを翻し、手には古びた杖を持っている。その姿はどこか浮世離れしており、明らかに異邦人だ。

「貴様、ここで何をしていた？」

男性の声は低く、しかし澄んでいた。驚いたことではない。私は最初から、彼が来ることを予期していたのだ。
霧の峡谷へ足を踏み入れた者とは、必ず誰かと繋がっている。そして、その繋がりこそが、私が孤独であるための唯一の理由でもある。

私は微笑んだ。顔はないので、表情の変化は見えないかもしれないが、心の中で深く頷いた。
「ご用件は何ですか？ 私、今ちょうどお茶の時間なんですけれど」

男性は眉をひそめた。彼の瞳は、深い森のような緑色をしている。
「お茶だと？ 人間ならぬ貴様が、何の冗談だ」

「冗談ではありませんよ」
jp.translation_en:
Especially here, in the misty gorge of Mistral Dale.

It is a place on no map, where wind and cloud always cross. People of the outer world call it "the cursed land of death" and go around it. But to me it is close to paradise, because here no one has any way of knowing what I really am.

"...That sound again."

Deep in my chest, where there should be no ribcage, a faint unease ran through me. The old enchanted tools were sounding a warning on their own. It was not an omen of disaster, only a signal that someone was nearby.

I stood and put my hand on the tea set on the desk (metal vessels, of course, that never need warming). I took my gaze off the floor and moved it to the little garden in the middle of the room. There bloomed the pale-blue flowers I had painstakingly raised out of the mist. My enchantments are used only to give the flowers strength and keep them from withering. No purpose beyond that. That was my definition of the slow life I wanted.

But I saw a black shadow squirming, coiled around the stems of those flowers.

"...Ah, there it is."

Even without speaking aloud, the other party surely sensed me. From beyond the mist, from the direction of a stone building like a ruin, a man appeared. He swept back a black cloak and held an old staff. There was something otherworldly about him; clearly a stranger.

"You. What were you doing here?"

The man's voice was low but clear. It did not surprise me; I had expected him from the start. Anyone who sets foot in the misty gorge is always tied to someone. And that tie is also the only reason I am alone.

I smiled. I have no face, so the change of expression may not show, but in my heart I nodded deeply. "What can I do for you? It happens to be my tea time."

The man frowned. His eyes were green, like a deep forest. "Tea? What kind of joke is that, from a thing like you that isn't human?"

"It isn't a joke."

jp.title: 婚約破棄された結界師、魔法学園で失われた魔法を取り戻す
jp.text:
「わたくしのような、ただ守るだけの役立たずには、もう必要ありません」

　冷たい言葉が、貴族の娘であるエルゼ様の瞳から零れ落ちた。
　その瞬間、わたくしの胸を締め付けたのは、悲しみというよりは、底なしの虚無感だった。

　婚約者であった公爵家の嫡男、カイル様もまた、わたくしに背を向けた。
「君の魔力は攻撃に使えない。剣を振るうこともできぬ。わたくしの戦いに、君は必要ないのだ」

　周囲の貴族たちの嘲笑が耳に残っている。
　かつて、この大陸の希望と呼ばれた魔法使いの一人として、わたくしは騎士団と共に歩んでいた。しかし、ある事件をきっかけに、わたくしの持つ『結界』の術式は、戦闘用の攻撃魔法と区別されることとなったのだ。
　防御のみを司るわたくしの存在は、軍隊において「足手まとい」として切り捨てられた。

　すべてを失ったわたくしは、故郷を追われ、辿り着いたのが聖ルミナス魔法学園の裏庭だった。
　ここでは、名門の血統や強大な攻撃魔法が至上とされる。わたくしのような、ひっそりと結界を張り巡らせ、静かに世界を守る技術は、誰も求めようとはしなかった。

　学園生活は、孤独なものだった。
　昼間は図書室の隅で古い魔導書を読み、夜は寮の窓辺で月を眺めて過ごす。
　わたくしは、失われたと思っていた魔法を探し求めていた。
　もし、わたくしが再び、真の意味で「強さ」を手に入れられるとしたら。

　そんなとき、学園の広場で異変が起きた。
　練習試合の最中、予期せぬ暴走魔獣が現れたのだ。
　それは、通常の魔法では対処できない、漆黒の霧のような不定形の怪物だった。
　生徒たちがパニックに陥り、放たれる炎の矢や氷の礫は、怪物の体をかすめるだけで消えてしまう。
　攻撃魔法だけが通用する世界では、この状況は死地同然だった。

「逃げろ！　出口が塞がれている！」

　叫び声が響き渡る。
　わたくしは震える足を引きずり、怪物の前に立ち止まった。
　恐怖が全身を駆け巡る。けれど、それ以上に、守りたいという衝動が湧き上がっていた。

（……失われた魔法、か）

　わたくしは、胸の奥に眠っていた記憶の扉を開いた。
　それは、攻撃のために魔力を凝縮させるのではなく、万物の理を包み込むための、純粋な魔力の循環。
　結界は、単なる壁ではない。空間そのものを書き換え、侵入者を拒絶する『領域』なのだ。

「開けよ、世界の境界を。――『永劫の盾（エターナル・シールド）』！」

　わたくしが叫ぶと同時に、周囲の空気が凍りついた。
　魔力が血管を伝い、心臓を激しく叩く。
　視界が白く染まる。
　怪物が放とうとした破壊の波動が、わたくしの展開した巨大な幾何学模様の結界に触れた瞬間、音もなく霧散していった。

　衝撃波さえ感じさせない、完璧な防護。
　わたくしの魔力は、攻撃のための爆発ではなく、全てを包含し、隔離するための静かな圧力へと変わっていた。
　怪物は、わたくしの結界の中に閉じ込められ、自壊していった。

　静寂が訪れる。
　呆然と立ち尽くす生徒たち。彼らの目に映るのは、弱者として見下してきた少女ではなく、圧倒的な力を操る一人の結界師の姿だった。

「……これは、どういう魔法ですか？」

　誰かの問いかけに応えられないまま、わたくしは地面に膝をついた。
　指先から溢れる魔力の残滓が、微かな光となって揺らめいている。
　わたくしは、守るためだけに生きてきた。
　けれど、今度は違う。
　この学園で、この世界で、わたくし自身の手で、失われた誇りを取り戻したのだ。
jp.translation_en:
"Someone like me, who can only protect, is of no use anymore."

The cold words spilled from the eyes of Lady Else, a noble's daughter. In that moment, what squeezed my chest was not so much sadness as a bottomless emptiness.

My fiancé, Lord Kyle, heir of a ducal house, also turned his back on me. "Your magic cannot be used to attack. You cannot even swing a sword. In my battles, you are not needed."

The sneers of the surrounding nobles still ring in my ears. Once, as one of the mages called this continent's hope, I marched with the knights. But after a certain incident, the spells of my "barrier" came to be treated as different from combat magic. Governing only defense, I was cut loose from the army as "dead weight."

Having lost everything, driven from my homeland, I ended up in the back garden of the Holy Luminous Magic Academy. Here, a famous bloodline and powerful attack magic are supreme. No one wanted a craft like mine, quietly stretching barriers and protecting the world in silence.

Academy life was lonely. By day I read old grimoires in a corner of the library; by night I watched the moon from the dormitory window. I was searching for magic I believed had been lost. If only I could once again gain "strength" in the true sense.

Then something happened in the academy square. In the middle of a practice match, an unexpected rampaging magic beast appeared: a shapeless monster like pitch-black mist that ordinary magic could not handle. The students panicked; the arrows of fire and shards of ice they loosed only grazed its body and vanished. In a world where only attack magic works, this was as good as a death trap.

"Run! The exit's blocked!"

The shout rang out. I dragged my trembling legs forward and stopped in front of the monster. Fear raced through my whole body. But even more, an urge to protect welled up.

(...Lost magic, is it.)

I opened the door of a memory sleeping deep in my chest. Not condensing mana for an attack, but a pure circulation of mana that enfolds the principles of all things. A barrier is not a mere wall. It is a "domain" that rewrites space itself and rejects intruders.

"Open, boundary of the world. Eternal Shield!"

The moment I shouted, the air around us froze. Mana ran through my veins and pounded my heart. My vision went white. The instant the monster's wave of destruction touched the huge geometric barrier I had raised, it dissolved without a sound.

Perfect protection, without even a shockwave. My magic had become not an explosion for attack but a quiet pressure that contains and isolates everything. The monster, sealed inside my barrier, destroyed itself.

Silence fell. The students stood dumbfounded. What they saw was not the girl they had looked down on as weak, but a barrier mage wielding overwhelming power.

"...What kind of magic is that?"

Unable to answer the question, I sank to my knees. The remnants of mana spilling from my fingertips flickered as faint light. I had lived only to protect. But this time was different. At this academy, in this world, with my own hands, I had reclaimed my lost pride.

en.title: A Useless Summoner Wants a Quiet Life in a Desert Oasis
en.text:
"I’m not useless," I whispered to the wind, though my heart still trembled with the weight of my failure. The sandstorm howled across the dunes of Kiri, a relentless gray shroud that threatened to bury me once more. Three years ago, the Grand Archmage had called for heroes to slay the Dune Serpent. Instead, they summoned me—a boy with no mana, no spells, and only a broken stone tablet. They laughed when I refused to fight. They called me a mistake. But mistakes can find purpose if they have the will to dig.

Now, the desert oasis of Mizu sits before me, a jewel of green against the endless ochre. This is my slow life. Not the life of glory, but the quiet dignity of survival. I am no longer a summoner; I am a gardener. With sweat and patience, I coax life from the parched earth, building a sanctuary where others only see waste. The title of my existence has changed, from "Useless Summoner" to something far more powerful: Survivor.

A roar shakes the ground. The serpent approaches, its scales shimmering like obsidian glass. Fear grips me, cold and sharp. But then, a memory surfaces: the laughter of those who doubted me. I pick up my trowel. It is not a weapon, yet it holds the promise of growth. As the monster lunges, I do not draw a sword. I plant a seed. In this desert oasis, silence is not emptiness. It is potential. I smile, watching the first green shoot push through the dirt. This is my story. Not a tale of war, but of renewal. And I intend to bloom, even here, in the heart of the storm.

en.title: The Weakest Saint and the Abyssal Prince
en.text:
The rain in the Kingdom of Tessaly did not fall; it wept, a cold, grey sorrow that seeped into the marrow of my bones. I sat on the edge of the crumbling balcony of the Cathedral of Whispers, watching the clouds churn above the spires. They were dark today, heavier than usual.

"Is this how it ends?" I asked the wind, though I knew no answer would come. "With damp socks and a broken heart?"

A shadow detached itself from the darkness of the courtyard below. It moved with a grace that defied gravity, clad in armor that seemed to be forged from obsidian and starlight. He stopped ten paces away, his cape billowing around him like a storm cloud.

"You look pale, Piet," said a voice that sounded like velvet over jagged glass.

I looked up. Standing there was Prince Zeno, the so-called Abyssal Prince of the Void Realm. His eyes were voids themselves, deep pools of nothingness that held a strange, lonely intelligence. Around him, the air hummed with a low, dissonant frequency. He was a creature of high fantasy lore, a being born from the darkest corners of existence, yet here he stood, offering me a handkerchief embroidered with silver thread.

"I am always pale," I replied, pulling my cloak tighter. "It is a side effect of having zero mana. A magical nullity. In this world, Zeno, that makes me less than human."

Zeno tilted his head. "And in the world of the Abyss, you are an anomaly. A ghost in the machine."

He stepped closer, ignoring the puddles forming at his feet. "Why do you stay? You are the weakest saint in history. Your prayers carry less weight than a whisper against a gale. Why do you choose to remain tethered to this dying land?"

I sighed, looking out over the city. From this height, the lights of Tessaly were dim, struggling against the encroaching gloom. This was my life. A dark fantasy tale where the heroes failed, where the gods turned their backs, and where I was merely a spectator to my own mediocrity.

"Because someone has to remember what we lost," I whispered.

"What loss?" Zeno asked, his expression softening for a fraction of a second. "We have been alone for centuries. The Holy Order hunts me. The humans fear your name. Why seek memory when you can seek peace?"

"Peace is a luxury for those who haven't seen the abyss staring back," I said.

He reached into his cape and produced a small, crystalline orb. It pulsed with a faint, dying light. "This was once part of the Sunstone Relic. My father took it from the Temple of Light before he fell. It was supposed to be a symbol of hope. Now, it is just a fragment."

I took the orb. It was warm, vibrating against my palm. "Hope is difficult to hold onto when you are weak, Zeno."

"Then let me help you hold it," he said.

Before I could refuse, the ground shook. The sky tore open, not with lightning, but with a scream of tearing fabric. From the rift emerged the Vanguard of Shadow, legions of armored knights wielding blades of pure entropy. Their leader, a towering figure in black plate, raised a sword that drank the light around it.

"Saint Piet!" Zeno shouted. "The ritual is complete! The breach is stable!"

The knights lunged. I felt the familiar, crushing weight of my lack of magic. My body screamed in protest, every nerve ending crying out for strength that wasn't there. I tried to raise a shield, but my hands trembled too violently to even summon a spark.

The leader’s blade descended. Time seemed to slow. I saw the fear in the eyes of the few guards remaining on the balcony, and I saw the profound sadness in Zeno’s gaze. He was readying a spell, a massive burst of abyssal energy meant to seal the rift, but it required a sacrifice. A conduit. Someone whose soul could withstand the backlash without shattering.

"Piet," Zeno said, his voice calm amidst the chaos. "You are the only one who can bridge the two worlds. Your weakness... it is the perfect balance."

I looked at the orb in my hand. It glowed brighter now, reacting to the encroaching darkness. I looked at Zeno, the prince of hell, who had chosen to stand beside me rather than rule over the world from afar. He didn't want my power. He wanted my presence.

"I won't die alone," I said.

"No," Zeno agreed, stepping forward. "But you will not be alone either."

I closed my eyes and opened myself to the void within me. Not the void of magic, but the void of empathy. I poured my will, my memories, my very essence into the crystal orb. I became the bridge. I became the anchor.

As the first blow struck, the world exploded in a flash of white light. I felt pain, yes—a searing, burning agony that threatened to unmake me—but beneath it was a strange, beautiful warmth. The darkness of the knight’s blade shattered against the light of the Orb. The rift snapped shut.

Silence returned to the cathedral, heavier than before.

When my vision cleared, I lay on the cold stone floor. The rain had stopped. The sun, hidden behind the clouds, cast a single beam of golden light onto my face.

Zeno knelt beside me. He was bleeding, his armor cracked, his eyes dull. But he was alive.

"Did we win?" I croaked, my voice thin.

"We survived," he corrected gently. He pressed a hand to my forehead, checking for fever. "That is a victory in itself, Saint."

I smiled, a weary, bittersweet expression. I had spent my life searching for purpose, believing that greatness came from power. Instead, I found it in the quiet moments, in the shared silence, in the simple act of standing by someone else’s side.

"Come inside, Prince," I whispered, reaching out for his hand. "The tea is getting cold."

He took my hand, his touch cool and comforting. Together, the weakest saint and the abyssal prince, walked toward the light. The world was still dark, and the monsters remained, but for the first time, it didn't feel quite so empty.

en.title: A Kicked-Out Summoner Wants a Quiet Life in the Frontier
en.passage: "The contract is void, Elian. Pack your bag." The words hung in the sterile air of the Royal Academy’s summoning hall, heavy as lead. I stood frozen, my hands still trembling from the mana backlash that had just torn through the ritual circle. The High Priestess, Lady Veyra, didn’t even look at me. She was busy wiping a smudge of soot from her pristine white robes with a handkerchief made of silk finer than anything a frontier farmer could afford. "But I tried," I whispered, my voice cracking. "I pulled three elements together. Water, Wind, and... Earth." "Elemental cohesion requires stability, not desperation," Veyra said, finally turning her gaze to me. Her eyes were cold, polished gemstones. "You are a Summoner, Elian. Not a firework display.
en.text: Your magic lacks precision. It is chaotic. Unreliable. And frankly, embarrassing for the Academy's reputation." She stepped closer, tapping my chest lightly with a slender finger. "You are hereby dismissed from the Third Year class. You will no longer attend classes, nor shall you receive further tuition fees. Go to the capital's outskirts. Live a quiet life. Do not bring your unstable gifts near the royal wards again." My heart felt like a stone dropping into a deep well. Dismissed. The word echoed louder than the crackling fire in the hearth. All my dreams of becoming a Grand Magus, of studying the ancient runes of the Great Library, shattered into dust. I looked down at my hands. They were scarred, the skin raised and pale where the raw mana had burned through my palms. I wasn’t a hero. I wasn’t a genius. I was a mistake. "Understood," I said. My voice was flat. I turned away before I could see her reaction, clutching my single satchel to my side. The walk from the academy gates to the borderlands was a blur of gray sky and damp cobblestones. I kept my head down, trying to ignore the whispers of students passing by. *Poor Elian. Can’t even summon a simple flame without hurting himself.* *They say he’s cursed. That he’ll burn everything he touches.* I didn’t care. If they called me a curse, then I would be a curse. At least, it meant they wouldn’t expect anything more from me. Three days later, I found myself standing at the edge of the Verdant Frontier. It was a place where the high fantasy of the capital met the gritty reality of the wild. Here, magic wasn’t studied in hushed halls; it was used to clear brambles, ripen crops, and ward off wolves. I rented a small, dilapidated cottage on the outskirts of the village of Larkspur, a hamlet so far removed from the politics of the Crown that even the royal messengers rarely passed through here. The cottage was small, smelling faintly of old wood and dried herbs. It had a thatched roof that leaked when it rained and a chimney that perpetually smoked because I hadn’t gotten around to fixing the damper yet. But it was mine. Or rather, it was empty. For a week, I did nothing but stare at the walls. I ate bread and cheese until I was sick. I sat by the window and watched the villagers go about their lives—the blacksmith hammering iron, the baker kneading dough, the children playing tag in the dirt. They were normal. Mundane. Peaceful. They didn’t need grand spells to survive. They needed patience and hard work. On the eighth day, hunger forced my hand. I needed food. Real food. Not the stale crackers from my bag. I wandered into the village market, feeling like an outsider among the colorful banners and shouting merchants. My clothes were stained, my hair was messy, and my eyes held the hollow look of someone who had been rejected by society. But as I picked up a loaf of fresh sourdough, I realized something strange. The air here felt different. Thicker. More alive. I wasn’t surrounded by the suffocating weight of expectation anymore. There was no one judging my lack of talent. There was only the smell of rain on dry earth and the promise of a simple meal. I decided then and there. I wouldn’t try to be a Grand Magus. I wouldn’t try to fix my magic or prove its worth to anyone. I would use it, quietly and secretly, to help this village thrive. I began by clearing the overgrown gardens behind the bakery, using small pulses of earth magic to break up the soil instead of the massive, uncontrolled bursts that had once terrified the priests. It was slow work. It was tiring. But every time a seed sprouted under my touch, I felt a warmth in my chest that had nothing to do with mana. It was satisfaction. It was peace. One afternoon, while harvesting turnips in the muddy fields, a storm rolled in. It wasn’t just rain; it was a magical tempest. Dark clouds gathered, swirling with jagged bolts of violet lightning that smelled of ozone and ancient power.

en.title: Secrets of the Academy in the Frontier
en.text:
"Stop staring at that floating crystal like it’s a lost puppy, Kaya."

The voice came from behind me, laced with a familiar, weary amusement. I didn’t turn around. I couldn’t. If I turned, I would have to admit that the glowing, pulsating blue orb wasn’t just a classroom prop; it was the only thing keeping my heart from shattering into a million pieces.

I gripped my staff tighter, my knuckles white. "It’s not a puppy, Ren-san. It’s a mana resonance core. And it’s leaking energy. If we don’t stabilize it, the entire West Wing will collapse."

Ren sighed, stepping up beside me. He was tall, broad-shouldered, and wore the pristine white uniform of the Arlo Academy for Magical Arts with an air of effortless grace. He looked every bit the star student, the golden boy who had already secured his place in the top tier of the university. To the rest of the student body, he was perfection. To me, he was the man who had chosen a quiet life as a researcher rather than joining the Vanguard, leaving me here alone in the dusty library archives while he went off to adventure.

"The Resonance Core isn’t leaking," Ren said softly, his eyes scanning the object. "It’s singing. Just listen."

I flinched. The humming vibration against my fingertips felt like a heartbeat. In this world, magic wasn’t just about casting spells; it was about understanding the rhythm of the world itself. Most students treated magic as a tool—a weapon to be honed, a power to be conquered. But I had spent years studying the forgotten texts, looking for the secrets buried beneath the surface of our rigid curriculum.

This was the bittersweet truth of my life here: while others chased glory in the Adventurer Guilds beyond the academy gates, I stayed behind, digging through the ruins of ancient knowledge to find peace. I wanted nothing more than a slow life, a quiet existence where I could tend to my small garden and study without the pressure of expectations. But the secrets of this academy were not meant to be ignored. They were whispering to me, pulling me deeper into the shadows.

The floor beneath us trembled. Dust rained down from the high ceiling, coating my hair like gray snow.

"Kaya!" Ren shouted, his composure cracking. He grabbed my arm, his grip firm but gentle. "The mana density is spiking! We need to evacuate!"

Panic surged through me, cold and sharp. I looked at the crystal. It wasn’t just glowing anymore; it was screaming in light. The air grew thick, heavy with the scent of ozone and old parchment. This was no accident. Someone had disturbed something deep within the foundations of the school.

"No!" I cried out, pushing myself forward. "If we leave, the containment spell will fail! The explosion won’t just take the wing; it’ll trigger a localized rift in the ley lines!"

Ren stared at me, disbelief warring with fear in his eyes. "That’s impossible. That’s forbidden theory. Why do you care so much?"

"Because I know what’s inside!" I yelled back, tears stinging my eyes. "I found the journals. They say the Academy wasn’t built on land. It was built on a seal. And someone has cracked it!"

A bolt of violet lightning arced from the ceiling, striking the corner of the room. The shockwave threw us backward. I landed hard, my breath knocked out of me, the staff skittering across the stone floor. Ren rolled toward me, checking for injuries before looking at the chaos erupting around us.

The floating crystal shattered, not with a bang, but with a silent, blinding flash of white light. As the light faded, the walls dissolved. Instead of stone corridors, we were standing on the edge of a precipice, overlooking a landscape that shouldn’t exist. Giant, crystalline trees reached toward a sky filled with twin moons. A massive, winged silhouette circled overhead, its shadow blotting out the stars.

We weren’t in the archive anymore. We were in the middle of the frontier, right where the academy met the void between worlds.

I looked at Ren. He was trembling, his hand hovering near his own wand, unsure how to cast a spell that would pierce this reality. He was the adventurer, trained to face monsters, yet he looked utterly lost in the face of cosmic horror.

"We can’t go back," I whispered, my voice barely audible over the whistling wind. "Not now."

I stood up, brushing the dust from my robes. My fear hadn’t vanished, but it had been replaced by a strange, exhilarating clarity. This was the secret I had been searching for all these years—the reason why the magic felt so hollow when cast traditionally. The academy was a cage, and I had finally found the key.

"Then we go through," I said, picking up my staff. It hummed in response to my command, pulsing with a newfound strength.

Ren blinked, then let out a shaky laugh. "You really are hopeless, Kaya. Always diving headfirst into the unknown."

"Well," I smiled, looking out at the endless, beautiful danger of the frontier. "Someone has to keep the slow life interesting."

Together, we stepped off the edge, falling not into darkness, but into the dawn of a new world.
